s: Marseille's 'Good Mother', watching from a scarred tower
w: Locals call her la Bonne Mere; her gilded Madonna has watched the Old Port from this 149-metre limestone outcrop since 1853. Built over an old fort as an enlarged medieval chapel, the basilica mixes a rock-carved Romanesque crypt with a mosaic Neo-Byzantine nave, its stonework still scarred by Liberation-era bullets.
_facts: Catholic basilica, Marseille's best-known symbol, known locally as la Bonne Mere
Built on the foundations of an old fort at the highest point of the city, on a 149m limestone outcrop; construction began 1853
Combines a rock-carved Romanesque crypt with a Neo-Byzantine mosaic upper church
Restoration 2001-2008 addressed stonework hit by bullets during the Liberation of France

s: Where a whole cluster of galaxies got its name
w: In 1877, director Edouard Stephan pointed his instruments at the sky and found a knot of galaxies now known as Stephan's Quintet. The old Palais Longchamp site still holds a planetarium added in 2001, plus a relic of the breakthrough: Foucault's glass-mirror telescope, forerunner of every reflecting telescope since.
_facts: Astronomical observatory with history back to the early 18th century
In 1877, director Edouard Stephan discovered the galaxy group Stephan's Quintet here
Old Palais Longchamp facilities are a noted tourist attraction; planetarium added 2001
Holds Foucault's glass-mirror telescope, forerunner of modern reflecting telescopes

s: Marseille's own archipelago, a short boat ride out
w: Four islands sit just four kilometres off Marseille's coast, technically still part of the city's 7th arrondissement despite barely 150 residents between them all. Pomegues and Ratonneau, two of the four, have been linked since 1822 by the Digue de Berry, a stone mole built to tame the crossing between them.
_facts: Archipelago of four islands about 4km off Marseille, part of the city's 7th arrondissement
Total land area around 200 hectares; population 146 in 2015 census
Pomegues and Ratonneau islands connected since 1822 by the Digue de Berry mole

n: Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations
w: Opened in 2013, the year Marseille wore the crown of European Capital of Culture, this national museum of European and Mediterranean civilisations pulled in 8.5 million visitors in its first three years and picked up the Council of Europe Museum Prize in 2015, proof the gamble on culture as regeneration paid off.
_facts: National museum (Mucem) inaugurated 7 June 2013 for Marseille-Provence 2013, European Capital of Culture
Won the 2015 Council of Europe Museum Prize
Welcomed 8.5 million visitors between 2013 and 2016, including 2.2 million in its exhibition spaces

s: Ancient Marseille, hiding behind a shopping mall
w: Walk into the Centre Bourse shopping arcade and you can walk out the back into the Jardin des Vestiges, a garden of classical ramparts, port buildings and a necropolis, uncovered when the site was dug up in 1967. The museum built around them reopened fully renovated for Marseille's 2013 Capital of Culture year.
_facts: Local historical and archaeological museum, opened 1983
Built around archaeological finds excavated in 1967 during construction of the Centre Bourse shopping arcade
Opens onto the Jardin des Vestiges outdoor garden with classical ramparts, port buildings and a necropolis
Completely renovated and reopened 14 September 2013 for Marseille-Provence 2013

s: The arena where Toto recorded a live album, on a whim
w: An 8,500-seat indoor amphitheatre that has hosted a genuinely strange cross-section of music history: Beyonce and Rihanna in the 2000s, Oasis at their peak, and Toto, who liked the room enough to record their 1999 live album Livefields inside it.
_facts: Indoor amphitheatre, capacity 8,500
Hosted concerts by Beyonce, Rihanna and Oasis, notably in the 2000s
Toto recorded their live album Livefields there in 1999

s: A Sephardi synagogue on Rue Breteuil, listed since 2007
w: Tucked onto Rue Breteuil in the 6th arrondissement, the Great Synagogue serves a congregation that worships in the Sephardi rite, a reflection of Marseille's deep Mediterranean and North African Jewish roots. The building itself was formally listed as a monument historique in 2007.
_facts: Jewish congregation and synagogue on Rue Breteuil, 6th arrondissement of Marseille
Listed as a monument historique in 2007
Congregation worships in the Sephardi rite

s: A chateau turned museum, its original decor still intact
w: Standing at the edge of Borely park in southern Marseille, this chateau has been a listed historical monument since 1936 and now houses the Museum of Decorative Arts, Earthenware and Fashion, its original interior decor still largely in place behind the exhibits since the museum moved in for Marseille-Provence 2013.
_facts: Chateau in southern Marseille, associated with Borely park
Listed as a historical monument since 1936
Houses the Museum of Decorative Arts, Earthenware and Fashion since Marseille-Provence 2013, with rich original decor
